shortDescription: Russia's manufacturing sector contracted in August for the first time in three months as output and new orders both fell amid weak client demand, a business survey showed on Tuesday.

children: Russia's manufacturing sector contracted in August for the first time in three months as output and new orders both fell amid weak client demand, a business survey showed on Tuesday.
The S&P Global Russia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to 48.8 in August from 50.7 in July. The 50 mark separates growth from contraction.

New orders returned to contraction after two months of growth, with firms citing weak client demand and reduced customer liquidity. New export business fell for a 10th straight month and posted its second-steepest decline since last September.

Production also declined for the first time since April, though only marginally, as lower order inflows weighed on activity. Employment fell again, with the pace of job shedding the fastest in three months as firms reported redundancies and did not replace voluntary leavers.

Price pressures intensified in August. Input cost inflation accelerated for a second month to its highest since January, driven by fuel and imported goods prices, while output price inflation quickened to a seven-month high as firms passed on higher costs.

Although business confidence improved from July's 74-month low, optimism remained below the long-run average. Firms linked expectations for higher output over the coming year to hoped-for stronger demand, advertising investment and competitive pricing.
